children: Commodity markets traded mixed on September 16, with oil prices falling on a surprise rise in US crude inventories, while gold remained steady after a two-day decline as investors awaited the Federal Reserve’s policy decision.

Oil prices fell on Wednesday after an unexpected build in U.S. crude inventories, while investors assessed supply risks after Saudi Arabia suspended oil loadings at its Yanbu port following an attack on its East-West pipeline to the Red Sea.
Brent crude futures fell 93 cents to $107.82 a barrel, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate futures were down 97 cents at $104.86 a barrel.
Both benchmarks settled more than $3 higher and at their highest levels since May 19 on Tuesday, as the Yanbu loading suspension stoked supply concerns and Saudi Arabia cut oil shipments to Europe.

In precious metals, gold was steady after a two-day drop as high oil prices continued to fuel inflation concerns and keep interest-rate hike bets a near-certainty ahead of the Federal Reserve’s policy decision later Wednesday.

Bullion was trading around $4,290 an ounce. Elevated energy prices pushed bond yields higher, and traders are now pricing in a 92% chance of the Fed hiking rates. Higher borrowing costs are typically negative for gold, which doesn’t pay interest.
Silver was little changed at $63.68 an ounce, while Platinum dipped 0.2% and palladium was up 0.1%.
The dollar inched up to trade near a two-week high on Tuesday as surging oil prices lifted Treasury yields and reinforced expectations that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates this week.
The dollar index, which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies, was last at 99.55.

title: Commodity Corner: Oil prices fall on US inventory build; gold steady ahead of Fed decision
